gfi_title: Decision matrix for seafood target species selection
scope_note: Human-food alternative seafood across platforms; a decision tool, not a product
vietnam_evidence: Applied to Vietnamese species: pangasius (1,938.8 kt farmed 2025; farm gate VND 26,500 to 30,000/kg; six catfish cell-line papers, all virology); shrimp (no true continuous line); grouper and Asian seabass (farmed under the 200 kt marine finfish target for 2030; food-oriented muscle lines published abroad in 2024 and 2025)
verdict_note: Adds a species choice to T8: target Asian seabass or grouper muscle cells; keep pangasius only as a low-cost model; defer shrimp. For hybrid and plant routes the matrix points to fish-paste formats (surimi species, snakehead, pangasius side streams). A full open tool is not needed for Vietnam; a one-page matrix in T8 is enough
signal_to_watch: Farm-gate prices and output of grouper and Asian seabass in Vietnam; a serum-free tropical marine muscle line
source_ids: GSD-01; MAC-15; FM-11; AQF-01; SLS-13; SLS-14; SLS-15; SLS-16; SCI-10; SCI-12; COST-47

vietnam_evidence: No route for cultivated food in Vietnam; no cultivated seafood approved for human food in Asia; no domestic demand before the mid-2030s (TPP-10); raw-fish sushi is not a Vietnamese mass format
verdict_note: A showcase belongs where approvals exist (Singapore, US). Vietnam would gain nothing from building it first
signal_to_watch: First cultivated seafood sold raw (sushi or sashimi) in Singapore, Japan or Korea

gfi_title: Scaffolding development for culinary and biomechanical requirements of cultivated seafood
scope_note: Cultivated seafood scaffolds for human food
vietnam_evidence: No Vietnamese scaffold work for fish found; scaffold materials in general are screened by L3 (GFI-085, GFI-094, GFI-109). Lab-grown seabass micro-tissue on scaffolds was made in India in 2025
verdict_note: Vietnam would use published scaffold methods in any T8 project, not develop them
signal_to_watch: A cultivated whole-cut fish product approved anywhere; open-access fish scaffold data with cooking texture

gfi_title: Understanding uptake and interconversion of omega-3 fatty acids by cultivated fish cells
scope_note: Cultivated seafood nutrition for human food
vietnam_evidence: Freshwater species such as pangasius can make some EPA and DHA from ALA; marine species such as grouper and seabass need them supplied. Pangasius oil holds only 0.17 to 0.31% EPA plus DHA
verdict_note: Relevant to the T8 species choice (marine targets cost more to enrich) but basic research Vietnam would buy
signal_to_watch: Published EPA and DHA uptake data for a tropical marine muscle line

gfi_title: Affordable animal-free omega-3 ingredients for alternative seafood and other alternative protein applications
scope_note: Omega-3 for human-food alternative seafood; feed omega-3 is context only (RM-07)
vietnam_evidence: VAST Institute of Biotechnology holds DHA thraustochytrid strains (S. mangrovei PQ6: 105.25 g/L biomass, 43.40% lipid in a 30 L fed-batch run; Aurantiochytrium SC145); no commercial algal omega-3 production found; domestic fish oil is not an omega-3 source
verdict_note: Vietnam would buy algal oil for any alternative seafood. The VAST strains are a research asset (see L2 strain-library question) and a possible later T5 tolling customer, not a play. Surimi-type products need no added omega-3
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese licence or pilot for food-grade DHA oil from a local strain; landed price of algal DHA oil for food

gfi_title: Novel methods for long-chain omega-3 fatty acid production
scope_note: Omega-3 production methods for human food
vietnam_evidence: No Vietnamese work on precision-fermentation or cell-free omega-3 found; only native thraustochytrid strains
verdict_note: Basic and strain-engineering research done abroad; Vietnam would buy the oil
signal_to_watch: A commercial fermentation-made EPA oil relaunched for food

gfi_title: Preventing oxidation of omega-3 fatty acids before and after addition to alternative seafood products
scope_note: Product quality of omega-3-enriched alternative seafood
vietnam_evidence: Hot climate and uneven cold chains raise oxidation risk, but no Vietnamese alternative seafood with added omega-3 exists
verdict_note: Generic food science; relevant only if a Vietnamese product adds omega-3, which SLS-C1 does not need
signal_to_watch: An omega-3-enriched alternative seafood launched in Southeast Asia

scope_note: Cultivated seafood nutrition for human food
vietnam_evidence: No Vietnamese cultivated seafood work; marine target species (grouper, seabass) would need EPA and DHA added
verdict_note: A cost item T8 should note, not a Vietnamese research priority
signal_to_watch: Published cost of EPA and DHA enrichment per kg of cultivated fish

gfi_title: Life Cycle Assessment for alternative seafood relative to conventional fishing and aquaculture
scope_note: Environmental evidence for human-food alternative seafood
vietnam_evidence: Vietnamese conventional LCAs exist (intensive pangasius 2011; Asian aquaculture including Vietnam 2015). Since GFI wrote, a Singapore LCA found 8.94 kg CO2 eq per kg for a surimi fish cake against 4.11 to 5.36 for a brown rice protein fish cake
verdict_note: Vietnam has no alternative seafood to assess. SLS-C1 can reuse the Singapore method if an EU buyer asks for a product footprint
signal_to_watch: EU or Japanese buyers asking for product carbon footprints on fish cakes

gfi_title: Promoting stemness and proliferation in fish cell cultures
vietnam_evidence: Warm-water lines grow faster (Asian seabass embryonic-stem-like line: 42 hours doubling at 28 C, as tabulated by GFI); no Vietnamese fish cell culture for food found
verdict_note: Supports choosing tropical marine species in T8; Vietnam would use, not develop, proliferation methods
signal_to_watch: Serum-free doubling under 24 hours in a tropical marine muscle line

gfi_title: Consumer and sensory research to guide alternative fish R&D
scope_note: Consumer and sensory research for human-food alternative fish
vietnam_evidence: Part III covers consumers generally; thịt nhân tạo (artificial meat) is a loaded name; no Vietnamese sensory study of fish analogues found. Plant chả cá chay already sells
verdict_note: General alternative-fish consumer research is not needed now. A narrow sensory panel of hybrid chả cá at 10 to 30% substitution is built into SLS-C1's kill tests
signal_to_watch: Any Vietnamese brand launching a fish analogue beyond chả cá chay

gfi_title: Cell line development from food-relevant aquatic species
scope_note: Cultivated seafood cell lines for human food
vietnam_evidence: No fish or shrimp line developed in Vietnam. Catfish lines (India, Taiwan) are virology lines. Food-oriented muscle lines now exist for seven-band grouper (Pukyong National University, 2024) and Asian seabass (Thiruvalluvar University, 2025), both relevant to species farmed in Vietnam
verdict_note: Adds partners and a species switch to T8 and RM-14: work with Thiruvalluvar, Pukyong or James Cook University Singapore on seabass or grouper, hosted by Nha Trang University or RIA3. Catfish gill-line papers (2021, 2022) found by title for OQ-100; name still unconfirmed
signal_to_watch: A food-relevant muscle line deposited in a public repository for a species farmed in Vietnam
source_ids: GSD-01; SLS-13; SLS-14; SLS-15; SLS-16; SCI-10; SCI-11; SCI-12; RD-01

scope_note: Human food. The hybrid part is in scope and near term; cultivated and fermentation-made surimi are in scope but far off
vietnam_evidence: Surimi and fish-cake exports more than USD 344 million (2025); more than 100 exporters (DALU SURIMI, CASES, KICOIMEX lead); tropical surimi at USD 1.67 to 2.24/kg (2025); capture to fall from 3.83 Mt (2025) to 2.8 Mt (2030); exporters report raw-material shortages and IUU import problems; pangasius side-stream surimi made commercially; plant chả cá chay on shelves
verdict_note: SLS-C1: hybrid fish cakes, fish balls and fish tofu with 10 to 30% of fish protein replaced by plant protein, labelled with the fish share. Not a hybrid frozen surimi: that trade buys by gel-strength grade. Cultivated and fermentation-made surimi are not for Vietnam: GFI's best-case cultivated cost (USD 6.43/kg) is about 3 to 4 times Vietnamese surimi prices of USD 1.67 to 2.24/kg (our calculation)
signal_to_watch: A Vietnamese fish-cake maker running a substitution trial; Korean or Japanese minimum fish-content rules; an approved cultivated surimi or fish ball anywhere
